title: hyperMILL Job Setup Procedure
body: Standard procedure for hyperMILL job setup: 1) Model and machining technology selection, 2) NCS orientation, 3) Stock size and allowances, 4) NCS position, 5) Machining frames, 6) Names for joblist, milling/turning area, stock, material and machine. Source: hyperMILL_Manual-en.pdf page_count=1525

title: hyperMILL Turning Contour Procedure
body: Turning model workflow in hyperMILL: 1) Create the contour for the turning model as Feature → 2D contour, 2) Create a turning job for the desired machining operation (grooving, etc.). Default approach/retract feedrate = 5 mm/revolution for finishing operations. Source: hyperMILL_Manual-en.pdf

title: hyperMILL Manual Keyword Analysis
body: Keyword frequency analysis from hyperMILL_Manual-en.pdf (2.2M chars, 1525 pages): machining=4211, feed=2057, milling=1515, toolpath=1299, drilling=1033, turning=874, depth=414, cutting=412, tolerance=383, finishing=295, roughing=263, stepover=174, speed=114, rpm=31. Primary focus: milling and drilling operations with extensive toolpath documentation.

title: InventorCAM 2.5D Milling - CAM-Part Definition Workflow
body: Complete CAM-Part definition workflow: 1) Load Autodesk Inventor model, 2) Start InventorCAM (Milling > New), 3) Choose CNC-Machine controller, 4) Start Coordinate System definition, 5) Select model face for Z-axis, 6) Define CoordSys Data, 7) Define Stock model, 8) Define Target model, 9) Save CAM-Part data, 10) Close CAM-Part. Source: InventorCAM2024_2.5D_Milling_Training_Course.pdf

title: InventorCAM Face Milling Operation Setup
body: Face milling operation workflow: 1) Open CAM-Part, 2) Add Face Milling operation (right-click Operations > Add Milling Operation > Face), 3) Define Tool parameters, 4) Define Face depth, 5) Define technological parameters, 6) Save and Calculate, 7) Simulate to verify, 8) Add next operation. Source: InventorCAM2024_2.5D_Milling_Training_Course.pdf

title: Post Processor Training - Basic Configuration
body: Post processor configuration fundamentals: Define machine kinematics, set output format (G-code dialect), configure tool change sequences, set up coordinate system handling, define canned cycle output, configure coolant/spindle codes. Source: Post Processor Training Guide.pdf (314 pages)

title: hyperMILL 5-Axis Milling - Swarf Cutting Setup
body: 5-axis swarf cutting procedure: 1) Select ruled surface geometry, 2) Define tool axis orientation (surface normal or fixed), 3) Set lead/lag angles for entry/exit, 4) Define stepover as percentage of tool diameter, 5) Configure collision checking, 6) Set tilting limits for A/B axes, 7) Verify toolpath in simulation with machine model. Source: hyperMILL_Manual-en.pdf

title: hyperMILL Mill-Turn - Synchronization
body: Mill-turn synchronization procedure: 1) Define turning operations on main spindle, 2) Add milling operations with correct coordinate system, 3) Set synchronization points between channels, 4) Configure C-axis positioning for milling features, 5) Define B-axis indexing for angled features, 6) Verify clearances during sync movements, 7) Output to multi-channel post processor. Source: hyperMILL_Manual-en.pdf

title: MIT 10.34: Numerical Methods Course Summary
body: MIT OCW 10.34 (Fall 2015) - Numerical Methods Applied to Chemical Engineering. 29 lectures covering: newton, jacobian, gradient, hessian, optimization, linear system, eigenvalue, singular value, decomposition, interpolation, quadrature, integration, differentiation, ode, pde, boundary value, initial value, stability, convergence, error, tolerance, iteration, residual, sparse, matrix, vector, norm, finite difference, monte carlo, stochastic. 464 formulas extracted across categories: general (306), summation (80), differential (34), integration (28), optimization (9), linear_algebra (7).

title: Newton's Method for Nonlinear Systems
body: Newton-Raphson iteration: x_{n+1} = x_n - J^{-1}(x_n) * F(x_n), where J is the Jacobian matrix. For single variable: x_{n+1} = x_n - f(x_n)/f'(x_n). Quadratic convergence near root. Used in: SpeedFeedOrchestratorEngine for iterative parameter optimization, ChatterStabilityLobeEngine for stability boundary calculation. Source: MIT 10.34 Lectures 1-6.

title: ODE Integration Methods for CNC Physics
body: Runge-Kutta 4th order (RK4): k1=hf(t,y), k2=hf(t+h/2,y+k1/2), k3=hf(t+h/2,y+k2/2), k4=hf(t+h,y+k3), y_{n+1}=y_n+(k1+2k2+2k3+k4)/6. Used in: ThermalWearCouplingEngine for coupled ODE, ToolWearProgressionEngine for wear evolution, RegenerativeChatterEngine for time-domain simulation. Adaptive step size for stiff systems. Source: MIT 10.34 Lectures 28-35.
